correctness.rationale: Differentiating the exact first integral cancels the nonlinear velocity-square term; its even potential has finite gamma-integral ceiling and all subcritical levels are compact regular ovals. The physical-period kernel is derived by direct substitution. Its Laplace representation gives pointwise x-large asymptotics, a uniform bulk bound, and a separate integrable turning-layer bound; together these prove both high-amplitude growth laws. The time-preserving force series gives the coefficient (kappa-5 beta)/16, and continuity plus eventual divergence gives an interior strict period minimum for 5 beta > kappa. The supplied checker passes nine symbolic/numerical assertions but finite examples are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact nonglobal part of a motivated quintic-center classification has a finite energy ceiling yet a full amplitude-parametrized period annulus. The physical-time period changes from quadratic to logarithmic divergence at the natural beta=0 restoring-force boundary, and the nontrivial local coefficient forces multiple equal-period cycles in a concrete positive open sector. These address qualitative questions in period-function dynamics beyond the known global-center decay theorem.
